title: Runtime backpressure: split admission control thresholds by request class (short/long)
author: Peter Holtz
release_notes: Internal only: backpressure now supports separate admission thresholds for short vs long request classes to protect interactive latency under mixed workloads.
body: Problem: Under mixed workloads, long-context (prefill-heavy) requests can saturate runtime admission limits and inflate short/interactive queue latency. The prior admission controller treated all incoming requests the same and applied a single global queue+inflight threshold, which caused priority inversion-like behavior during bursts: a few long requests could consume the entire admission budget, forcing short requests to wait behind admission rather than letting them enter the short queue and be dispatched promptly by the mixed-workload scheduler. Change summary: This PR splits admission control thresholds by request class (short vs long) and applies distinct queue limits and inflight budgets. Short-class admission is protected by a reserved budget so that long-class bursts cannot fully consume capacity. Long-class admission still proceeds when capacity is available, and is rate-limited when it would cause short queue delay spikes. Implementation details: (1) AdmissionController now takes RequestClass (short|long|unknown) and uses class-specific watermarks: max_enqueued_by_class and max_inflight_by_class (prefill-stage inflight). (2) Unknown class is treated as long by default (conservative for short protection); can be overridden via config for specific routes/tiers. (3) Added backpressure reasons and metrics: runtime_admission_rejected_total{class,reason}, runtime_admission_queue_depth{class}, runtime_admission_inflight{class}, and runtime_admission_limit{class,kind}. (4) Added config plumbing behind the existing mixed workload feature flag; default behavior remains identical to baseline unless the scheduler prototype is enabled. (5) Tests: unit tests for watermark accounting + an integration-style overload test that reproduces the regression (short requests blocked by long inflight) and asserts short admission continues while long is throttled. Notes: This is intentionally scoped to admission/backpressure; dispatch policy changes remain in PR #8433/#8439. Risk/mitigation: Potential starvation of long requests if thresholds are misconfigured. Guardrail: we keep a non-zero long budget and expose gauges + alerts can be built on rejection rate and long queue depth growth. Follow-ups: wire rejection metrics into mixed-workload dashboards (ENG-4828) and validate thresholds in trace replay (ENG-4830).
commits: admission: plumb RequestClass into admission controller
config: add per-class admission thresholds (flag-gated) and defaults
metrics: emit rejection counters and per-class inflight/queue gauges
tests: add overload regression test for short-queue protection
docs: inline comments and config examples
checks: CI summary (required): build-linux-x86_64 (pass), unit-tests (pass), runtime-integration-tests (pass), lint (pass), clang-tidy (pass). Optional: perf-smoke (pass). Note: runtime-integration-tests failed once due to a flaky timing assertion in mixed_workload_overload_test; rerun passed after loosening the assertion window and switching to a percentile-based check.
conversation: Sofia Ivanova (review): "This makes sense for protecting short, but I want to ensure we don’t accidentally bypass the scheduler fairness window by rejecting too aggressively. Can you confirm the long class still makes progress under sustained mixed load? Also, where does 'unknown' land?" Peter Holtz (author): "Agree. Long budget remains non-zero (default 2 inflight prefill + 32 enqueued) and the long controller only throttles when long would exceed its own watermark; it does not depend on short queue depth. 'Unknown' defaults to long to avoid misclassifying heavy work as short; config supports treating unknown as short for known-safe routes." Omar El-Sayed (review): "Please add metrics with {class,reason} so we can separate long throttling from global overload. Also can we expose the configured limits as gauges?" Peter Holtz: "Added runtime_admission_rejected_total{class,reason} with reasons: enqueued_limit, inflight_limit, global_overload, and added runtime_admission_limit{class,kind} gauges (kind=enqueued|inflight)." Sean Gallagher (review): "SRE concern: a misconfig could starve long and we won’t notice until customers complain. Can we add a guardrail signal or test that long rejections don’t go to 100% under normal mixed workload?" Peter Holtz: "Added an integration test scenario where sustained traffic keeps both classes admitted; also exposed per-class queue depth + inflight gauges to drive alerting. We’ll incorporate paging thresholds in ENG-4828/rollout checklist." Benji Okafor (review): "Flag behavior: ensure default-off keeps exact prior semantics. Also do we need config migrations for existing clusters?" Peter Holtz: "Confirmed: if mixed-workload flag is disabled, controller uses the legacy single-threshold path. No migration needed; new keys are ignored unless enabled." Sofia Ivanova (approval): "Approved after the unknown-class default + metrics additions.
